Request service records 1917 - present Records for yourself or next of kin You can request service records for yourself or for your next of kin (spouse, parent, child, or sibling). pages.text: How to photograph the stars using your phone | National Geographic PHOTOGRAPHY How to photograph the stars using your phone Astrophotographer Sadeq Hayati spills his secrets to snapping stunning night sky images without a big, fancy camera. Using his phone, Hayati shot more than 120 consecutive photos in one night and combined them into this image showing the paths of stars above a monument in Iran. With the global celebrations for Sir David Attenborough’s 100 th birthday shining a light on the pioneering wildlife documentaries that first brought the magnificence of the natural world to our screens, you might be inspired to pick up a camera and head off on your own big adventure. But how to choose where to go, what to take with you and how to make the most of it once you get there? Where and when to go When it comes to wildlife safaris, Africa is unrivalled in terms of its variety. In this huge continent of savannahs, wetlands and national parks, most sub-Saharan safari destinations have their dry season between June and October, when the Big Five — lion, leopard, buffalo, rhino and elephant — congregate at water sources, making them easier to spot. But the tail end of the wet season is less crowded and arguably just as spectacular, with the bonus of dramatic skies and verdant grasslands. If it’s your first safari and you want to see it all, you can’t go wrong with East Africa. If you suspect someone stole your personal information or identity, placing a credit freeze can help protect you from fraud. What is a credit freeze? When you place a security freeze , creditors cannot access your credit report. This will keep them from approving any new credit account in your name, whether it is fraudulent or legitimate. To let lenders and other companies access your credit files again to create new accounts, you will need to lift your credit freeze permanently or temporarily. Annexed by an endless parade of empires — including the Greeks, Romans, Byzantines and Ottomans — in 1878, Cyprus became a British protectorate. These last rulers chose the lofty, leafy Troodos Mountains as their summer capital to escape the heat of the coast, and it’s still favoured by locals from spring to autumn. Cyprus became independent in 1960, but vestiges of its storied past are everywhere, from its ancestral grapes, mavro and xynisteri, to mural-washed churches hidden among the hills and turn-of-the-century mansions left by long-gone grandees. Scattered as if on a pirate’s map off England’s southwesterly tip, the Isles of Scilly aren’t a place you stumble over. Travellers need to have booked well ahead for the short, spectacularly scenic transfer by twin-prop plane or helicopter from Penzance to the 140-strong archipelago. Or embark on a three-hour, dolphin-flanked ferry, which plies azure waters towards show-off shelves of pristine white sand. It’s a pilgrimage richly rewarded by a landscape of palms, lipstick-pink sea thrift and sky-blue agapanthus flowers, framing sand-blown, barely-there roads. Beyond St Mary’s, the largest and most populous isle, there are few cars on the four other inhabited outposts of Tresco, Bryher, St Martin’s and St Agnes. They offer a daily invitation to hike and island-hop, with dockings dictated by the tides, and crossings taking mere minutes on jetboat ferries with names like Firethorn and Thunder. Home to the Aboriginal Palawa people for 40,000 years, Tasmania was settled by Europeans from 1803. They found a maritime climate, volcanic soils and some of the cleanest air in the world. These bountiful conditions have since helped the apple-shaped island build its reputation for producing superlative wine, whisky and cheese. On a road trip across Australia’s smallest state, preserved colonial-era towns and farms seem to appear around every corner, while mountains and valleys knitted together by walking trails provide chances to stretch your legs. Meanwhile, after centuries of oppression, the Palawa people invite visitors to connect with their ancestral homelands through the sights, sounds and flavours of the bush. You could easily drive coast to coast in six hours, but why rush? Tasmanians know that having patience and adopting a slower pace are key to enjoying the finer things in life. Along the way, make time to savour a drop of local whisky, perhaps sample oysters from a coastal farm fringed by white sand, head into the backcountry for a day’s wilderness walk, or spend time foraging with Aboriginal guides. Palm-fringed surf bays, tea plantation hikes, ancient ruins and incense-filled temples — few islands can match the diversity of Sri Lanka. First-timers tend to head south for beach-hopping and safaris, but the developing north offers an equally rich experience, along with an insight into the island’s Tamil culture. Here are two handpicked itineraries that show off the best of both sides of the island. Highlights of the South A classic circuit of the country’s southern half takes in highland tea plantations, Buddhist pilgrimage sites and heritage towns — as well as some of its finest surf hubs. 1. Kandy Best For: Temple Pilgrimages The last stronghold in Sri Lanka to fall to the British in 1818, Kandy was once a royal seat and remains an important cultural and religious centre. Enthroned in the lush highlands, the city has a large lake at its heart, with royal bathhouse ruins, tiny bee-eaters in the trees and vendors selling chilli-mango at its edges. Pilgrims come from all over the Buddhist world to attend the thrice-daily puja (worship) ceremony at the Temple of the Tooth, a bone-white complex that holds a relic of Buddha himself, protected by bristling walls of elephant tusks. How to Protect Yourself and Others Mar. 10, 2025 Español What to know CDC’s Respiratory Virus Guidance provides strategies you can use to help protect yourself and others from health risks caused by COVID-19 and other respiratory viruses. These actions can help you lower the risk of COVID-19 transmission (spreading or catching COVID-19) and lower the risk of severe illness if you get sick. Core Prevention Strategies CDC recommends that all people use core prevention strategies to protect themselves and others from COVID-19: Stay up to date with COVID-19 vaccines . Although vaccinated people sometimes get infected with the virus that causes COVID-19, staying up to date on COVID-19 vaccines significantly lowers the risk of getting very sick, being hospitalized, or dying from COVID-19. Practice good hygiene (practices that improve cleanliness) Take steps for cleaner air When you are sick: Use precautions to prevent spread , including staying home and away from others (including people you live with who are not sick) if you have respiratory symptoms. Report a lost or stolen military or veteran ID Common Access Card (CAC) Active-duty service members and civilian Department of Defense employees must report a lost or stolen Common Access Card (CAC). You must: Contact your command or local security office at your service duty station , or Call Military OneSource at 1-800-342-9647 Uniformed Services ID (USID) card USID cards are typically used by retired military members, reservists, and military dependents. pages.description: Scientists are employing AI-guided bioacoustics monitoring to discover how many critically endangered indri still exist in Madagascar's forests.
pages.text: How to Save the World’s Largest Lemurs? Listen to Their Songs. | National Geographic ANIMALS How to Save the World’s Largest Lemurs? Listen to Their Songs. Scientists are employing AI-guided bioacoustics monitoring to discover how many critically endangered indri still exist in Madagascar's forests. A male indri sings in Madagascar. These endangered lemurs have complex vocals that help them claim territory in the forest. Photographs by Filippo Carugati By Sruthi Gurudev Published October 22, 2026 The tropical rainforests of Madagascar are a raucous wash of sound, pierced by astonishingly loud, musical singing. These are the vocalizations of the indri , the largest species of lemur in the world. Emanating from up in the green-black canopy, the indri songs are notably mournful and resonant—partly whale song and partly wolf howl. They rise to a crescendo and then fall away into silence. For roughly 88 million years, Madagascar has been geographically isolated from Africa and Asia. Considered something of an “ evolutionary sandbox ,” the ancestors of many of its terrestrial mammals are thought to have reached the island from continental Africa, some floating on mats of vegetation carried by ancient ocean currents. Once there, isolated populations proliferated and diversified, producing unique wildlife found nowhere else on Earth. The indri is one such animal. Endemic to the island, the species is critically endangered ; they’re threatened by habitat loss caused in part by tavy , the slash-and-burn agriculture that destroys their arboreal habitat. pages.description: This year’s high solar activity means it’s a prime time to catch the Aurora Borealis — here’s how to spot this celestial phenomenon in and around the Alberta capital.
pages.text: How to see the Northern Lights in Canada's Edmonton region | National Geographic PAID CONTENT FOR EXPLORE EDMONTON TRAVEL How to see the Northern Lights in Canada's Edmonton region This year’s high solar activity means it’s a prime time to catch the Aurora Borealis — here’s how to spot this celestial phenomenon in and around the Alberta capital. Thanks to its northern latitude and clear night skies, Edmonton is a prime spot to view the auroras. Explore Edmonton By Brendan Sainsbury Published May 12, 2026 Nature’s most spectacular light show, the Aurora Borealis, will be even more dazzling this year. This is thanks to a phenomenon called the ‘solar maximum’, defined as the ‘peak’ of the sun’s activity over its 11-year cycle. One of the best places to take advantage of this astronomical event is in Edmonton — North America’s most northerly city, set at latitude of 53.5ºN. With a landscape of wide-open plains, Edmonton and the surrounding region offers a front-row seat to the wonders of the galaxy. Here’s how to spot the auroras using Alberta’s capital as your base. When should I go? Though the solar maximum technically occurred in 2024, this high period of solar activity is expected to continue well into 2026. Put simply, this means that the sun will be sending more electrically charged particles to Earth than usual. These then convert to green, red, purple and blue light when they collide with our atmosphere, which we see as the auroras. pages.title: How to spend a weekend in North Norfolk, UK | National Geographic
pages.description: Home to seals, rare birdlife and some of Britain’s best seafood restaurants, this part of East Anglia offers a peaceful break, with a coastal landscape of sand dunes and salt marshes.
pages.text: How to spend a weekend in North Norfolk, UK | National Geographic National Geographic Traveller (UK) content straight to your inbox — sign up for our newsletter here By Karlina Valeiko Published September 19, 2023 • 13 min read This article was produced by National Geographic Traveller UK. Drawing visitors since the 1700s, North Norfolk has long been a place of escapism. You arrive ready to fill your lungs with sea air and let your gaze drift to the horizon. The natural beauty here is not the kind that smacks you in the face and overwhelms with superlatives. The expansive beaches, endless skies, fenland and watery network of the Broads are a more subtle tonic for the soul — you don’t have to work too hard to forget life beyond this somewhat overlooked patch of East Anglia. It’s also a place to get closer to wildlife. Many of the salt marshes in Norfolk offer some of Britain’s best birdwatching, while seals love to sunbathe on the shingle spits at Blakeney Point. Plus, there’s bluebell and snowbell carpets in spring, dragonflies buzzing over lavender fields in summer and woodland ablaze in ochre, yellow and red in autumn. Beyond the pull of its natural attractions, North Norfolk is dotted with stately homes, sliced through by heritage railways and framed by historic towns. Add it all together and you have a region that promises the kind of serenity many search far and wide for, yet few expect to find so close to home. Tofino Harbour is the gateway to Clayoquot Sound's 60-mile-wide stretch of water, home to Tofino’s islands and inlets. Photograph by Francesco Riccardo Iacomino By Sarah Barrell Published May 16, 2025 This article was produced by National Geographic Traveller (UK). Set on Vancouver Island’s wild western shore, Tofino is a town surrounded by windswept beaches and coastal rainforest. It has a hippy air and is home to year-round surfers, Indigenous artists and an increasing number of chefs, drawn to the natural riches of the Pacific coast. The resplendent quetzal is considered one of the most beautiful birds in the world. The males can grow tail feathers that are up to a metre in length. Fomalhaut, one of the brightest stars in the autumn night sky, lies about 25 light-years from Earth. Roughly 15 times as luminous as our sun, the star is surrounded by vast belts of dust that may hold clues to planets astronomers have yet to discover. NASA, ESA, and the Digitized Sky Survey 2 By Stefanie Waldek Published October 23, 2026 On an autumn night in the Northern Hemisphere, Fomalhaut appears as a bright pinprick in a field of darkness, far from other bright stars. But the star’s apparent solitude is only part of its story: It sits at the center of an expansive system of dusty belts that may hold clues to worlds we have yet to find. The Congressional Record is the record of proceedings and debates on the floor of the U.S. House of Representatives and the U.S. Senate. It's published daily when one or both chambers of Congress are in session, and a permanent, bound edition is published after the end of each session of Congress. The Congressional Record first began publication in 1873, but it is preceded by three other publications: the Annals of Congress (1789-1824), the Register of Debates (1824-1837), and the Congressional Globe (1833-1873). While later volumes of the Congressional Globe began to provide something approaching verbatim coverage, most of these early publications only have paraphrased speeches, condensed reports, and summaries. For more background on these early publications, the Law Librarians' Society of Washington, DC has put together a helpful Overview of the Congressional Record and Its Predecessor Publications . The Congressional Record is freely available online via Congress.gov— the official website for U.S. federal legislative information, developed and maintained by the Library of Congress. Congress.gov has the daily Congressional Record issues dating from 1995, and then the bound edition from 1873 through 1994. But in conflict settings – like those in which the ICRC operates – the power dynamics between humanitarian organizations, local bodies and community members are mostly unbalanced, which hampers trust and collaboration. Being accountable to the people we serve makes it harder for this power asymmetry to be exploited.
